source: Zhang, Feng, Tan (2022) Active Example Selection for In-Context Learning
finding: Which demonstrations an LLM sees changes accuracy a lot. Random sets of 4 examples gave huge spread on GPT-2, even after reordering and calibration. This is the base problem a learned-value selector tries to fix.
numbers: 30 random sets of 4 examples, GPT-2: accuracy on the same task differed by more than 30 points. Worst set on TREC scored 10.0% (chance 16.7%). On AGNews best set 79.5% vs worst 26.1% (gap 53.4). Best of 24 orderings gave only +8.1% on average over random. For 9 of 30 TREC sets the best ordering was still below random examples.
limits: GPT-2 (345M) mostly; GPT-3 Ada/Babbage variance smaller and reduced by calibration. Classification only (AGNews, Amazon, SST-2, TREC).
agent_relevance: The choice of cases in context is a high-variance lever. A scaffold that picks cases blindly pays that variance as noise.

source: Zhang, Feng, Tan (2022) Active Example Selection for In-Context Learning
finding: They framed example selection as a sequential decision problem (choose k examples one at a time, reward = LM accuracy at the end) and learned a Q-function policy offline with off-policy data. On the same task the learned policy beat random but not a cheap oracle.
numbers: SAME TASK avg accuracy over AGNews/Amazon/SST-2/TREC (5 seeds): random 59.6, max-entropy 59.3, reordering 63.5, best-of-10 random draws 72.5, greedy oracle 78.0, learned policy 71.4 (seen examples), 71.6 (100 new examples), 69.0 (1000 new examples). Text: policy beats random/max-entropy/reordering by 11.8/12.1/7.9 points.
limits: Learned policy about equals best-of-10 random sampling, which needs a validation set. Features were deliberately minimal. Greedy oracle has exponential cost.
agent_relevance: If a validation signal exists, trying 10 random case sets and keeping the best nearly matches a learned selector. Learned value is not magic.

source: Zhang, Feng, Tan (2022) Active Example Selection for In-Context Learning
finding: Transfer of the learned policy to a new task was small, and transfer to bigger models faded. This is a boundary condition for learned case value.
numbers: NEW TASK (train on 3 tasks, test on 4th) avg: random 59.6, reordering 63.5, learned (100 candidate examples) 63.8, learned (1000 candidates) 65.4. Abstract: 5.8% average gain on new tasks. GPT-3 Ada: about +1%; mixed on Babbage and Curie. Limited gain over reordering.
limits: Gain over reordering is within the noise of the intervals shown (CIs up to +/-13 on single tasks). Authors say improvement shrinks on larger GPT-3 models.
agent_relevance: Learned value is task-specific. A value learned on one task family should not be trusted on another without re-validation.

source: Zhang, Feng, Tan (2022) Active Example Selection for In-Context Learning
finding: Surprise: label balance did not predict good demonstration sets. Sets with all-positive labels did better than balanced ones in sentiment.
numbers: Amazon: all 4 demos positive averaged 87.8% vs 83.3% for perfectly balanced sets (+4.5). SST-2: all-positive or all-negative had lower variance than balanced.
limits: Single small model (GPT-2); may not hold for current LLMs.
agent_relevance: Hand rules about case diversity or balance can be wrong. Value should be measured, not assumed.

source: Rubin, Herzig, Berant (2022) Learning To Retrieve Prompts for In-Context Learning (EPR)
finding: EPR learns a retriever from the LM own signal: score each candidate training example by the probability the LM gives to the correct output when that example is the prompt, label top-5 positive and bottom-5 negative, and train a contrastive dual encoder. This is learned case value by outcome (a one-step, offline form of a bandit reward).
numbers: Dev, GPT-Neo (BREAK NEM / MTOP EM / SMCalFlow EM): BM25 26.0/52.9/46.1; CBR (prior learned retriever) 25.7/57.0/51.4; EPR 31.9/64.2/54.3; BM25-oracle (uses gold output) 32.3/58.9/47.3. Test: BREAK BM25 17.6 vs EPR 23.9; MTOP BM25 49.0 vs EPR 64.4.
limits: Semantic parsing tasks where structure matters; candidates are first pruned by BM25, so EPR only re-ranks. Needs a labelled train set and many LM calls to build labels.
agent_relevance: Outcome-scored retrieval beats similarity most where the right case shares structure, not words. Our agent can use its own task results as the label.

source: Rubin, Herzig, Berant (2022) Learning To Retrieve Prompts for In-Context Learning (EPR)
finding: EPR beat even an oracle that uses the gold answer for BM25 on two of three datasets, so surface similarity to the answer is not what makes a case useful. Random prompts were near useless.
numbers: BREAK dev, full-context: RANDOM 1.7, BM25 26.0, DR-BM25 23.6, EPR 31.9, BM25-oracle 32.3 (one-shot: 1.1 / 15.2 / 14.1 / 23.0 / 18.0). Retriever trained on GPT-Neo signal transfers: EPR beats the best baseline by 2-8 points across LMs (GPT-J, GPT-3, Codex) on 1,000-example dev samples.
limits: Model behind the one-shot column not checked in my read. Single run per cell.
agent_relevance: Reward-trained retrieval generalises across LMs in this setup, so a value learned on a cheap model might carry to a stronger one.

source: Wang, Yang, Wei (2023) Learning to Retrieve In-Context Examples for Large Language Models (LLM-R)
finding: LLM-R refines the EPR idea: a reward model re-ranks BM25 candidates using LLM log-likelihood, a dense retriever is distilled from it, and the loop is iterated with mined hard negatives. Gains saturate after about two rounds.
numbers: Average over 30 tasks, LLaMA-7B, 8 examples: zero-shot 44.9, random 57.9, k-means 57.0, BM25 61.3, E5 61.4, SBERT 62.1, EPR 63.5, LLM-R iteration 1 65.7, iter 2 66.5, iter 3 66.4. Abstract claims +7.8% over random. NLI category: random 44.0, BM25 50.8, LLM-R (iter 3) 72.5.
limits: Iteration 3 is not better than 2. Std dev reported only for the random baseline over 3 runs. Many tasks are classification where input pattern matching is enough.
agent_relevance: Two rounds of re-scoring by outcome is the sweet spot. More rounds add nothing. A value-update loop should be short.

source: Wang, Yang, Wei (2023) Learning to Retrieve In-Context Examples for Large Language Models (LLM-R)
finding: Failure case: learned retrieval hurt on SQuAD and helped little on knowledge-heavy tasks. The retriever picked near duplicates with little diversity.
numbers: SQuAD v1: LLM-R below the random-selection baseline. Knowledge-intensive tasks (commonsense, memorised facts) show gains well below the 30-task average, NQ being the exception.
limits: Explanation by the authors from manual inspection (many questions share one passage), not a controlled test.
agent_relevance: Value learning can collapse onto redundant cases. A bandit needs an explore or diversity term, not only exploitation of the current best.

source: Ye et al. (2023) Compositional Exemplars for In-context Learning (CEIL)
finding: Scoring cases one by one misses interactions. CEIL models the whole set of examples with a conditional determinantal point process (relevance plus diversity), trained contrastively with LM feedback. Set-level selection beats per-item retrieval.
numbers: Ablation average (as printed in my text extraction): TopK with EPR 57.64, DPP-EPR 59.95, TopK-CEIL 60.73. Efficiency table: EPR avg 64.86 at 30s vs CEIL n=100 68.86 at 36s, n=800 69.32 at 118s. Tested on 12 classification sets plus generation and semantic parsing.
limits: PDF table layout was garbled; column labels inferred. Gains of 2-4 points average. Different task mix from the EPR paper.
agent_relevance: Choosing a set is a combinatorial bandit, not k independent arms. Diversity matters beyond individual case value.

source: Liu et al. (2021) What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3? (KATE)
finding: Early baseline: choosing in-context examples by nearest neighbours in sentence-embedding space beats random sampling, and encoders fine-tuned on related data help more. GPT-3 results swing a lot with random example choice.
numbers: NQ exact match: random 28.6 +/-0.3; best KATE variants about 41-42 (table columns partly garbled). WQ random 41.0; TriviaQA random 59.2; abstract: large gains on ToTTo (41.9) and NQ (45.5). SST-2 with encoder fine-tuned on SST-2: 93.43 vs 91.99 for plain RoBERTa. Fine-tuning on a dissimilar task can hurt.
limits: Which KATE column maps to which number is uncertain in my read. Gains largest on QA and table-to-text, small on easy sentiment.
agent_relevance: Similarity retrieval is the strong default. Any learned-value rule has to beat it, not random.

source: Min et al. (2022) Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
finding: Counter-finding that limits what a case-value signal can learn: replacing gold labels in the demonstrations with random labels barely hurts. The demos mostly convey format, input distribution and label space.
numbers: 12 models, 16 demos: random labels cost 0-5% absolute; 1.7% on average for multi-choice, 2.6% for classification. Gold demos significantly beat no demos.
limits: Mostly pre-GPT-4 era models and classification/multi-choice. Later work suggests larger models use labels more.
agent_relevance: If correctness of a case answer matters little, an outcome-based value for a case may mostly track format and topic fit, not truth.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Memento is the clearest LLM version of retrieval as a bandit. Case retrieval is a policy over a case bank, learned by maximum-entropy soft Q-learning: pi(c|s) is a softmax of Q(s,c)/alpha. Q is learned either by a kernel over states or by a small MLP over frozen SimCSE embeddings. The LLM stays frozen.
numbers: Case = (state, action, reward); only the final step of a trajectory is written to the bank; TD update Q <- Q + eta[r + gamma*alpha*log sum exp Q' - Q]. Planner GPT-4.1, executor o3 (GAIA) or o4-mini.
limits: Reward is sparse and binary (task success). It is a contextual-bandit-like or short-horizon RL view with a changing arm set.
agent_relevance: Directly maps to our selection slot: score each stored case by its learned value in context and sample with entropy so exploration persists.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: The learned (parametric) Q retriever beat plain similarity retrieval over five rounds, but only by a small margin. Both beat no case memory by a larger margin.
numbers: DeepResearcher learning curve (Table 4), iter1 to iter5: no CBR 78.65 -> 84.47; non-parametric similarity CBR 79.84 -> 84.85; parametric Q CBR 80.46 -> 85.44. Parametric minus similarity: +0.62 at iter 1, +0.59 at iter 5. CBR on top of planning: +6.7 F1 / +8.2 PM (DeepResearcher), +4.5/+7.0 (HLE), +3.7/+5.3 (SimpleQA).
limits: No confidence intervals or seeds reported. The case bank saturates after few passes (about 3k training items). The no-CBR line also rises, so most gain over rounds is not memory.
agent_relevance: Learned value adds under one point over cosine similarity here. The big win is having a case memory at all. Do not over-invest in the bandit layer.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Fewer retrieved cases is better. Gains peak at about 4 cases then plateau or fall, unlike few-shot prompting.
numbers: DeepResearcher avg F1/PM by number of cases K: K=0 59.9/72.2; K=1 63.6/77.9; K=2 63.7/78.1; K=4 64.5/78.5; K=8 64.1/78.2; K=16 63.9/78.1; K=32 63.9/78.1. Most of the gain (+3.7 F1) comes from the first case.
limits: Single configuration (GPT-4.1 planner, o4-mini executor). Differences from K=1 to K=4 are under 1 point.
agent_relevance: Retrieve few cases (1-4). The marginal case adds little and the first one matters most.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Out-of-distribution test and a contamination warning. Cases from NQ/TQ/HotpotQA/2Wiki helped on unseen datasets, but the paper notes that live tools without planning scored below the offline model on DeepResearcher.
numbers: OOD datasets MuSiQue, Bamboogle, PopQA: absolute gains 4.7 to 9.6 points with 4 retrieved cases. Table 5 DeepResearcher: offline executor 48.8/62.8 F1/PM, online executor 30.8/60.7 (-18.0 F1), Memento w/o CBR 59.9/72.2, Memento 66.6/80.4.
limits: Authors suspect training-data contamination of those benchmarks. Gains are against their own ablations, not independent replication.
agent_relevance: Case reuse transfers across question styles in QA. Check baselines for contamination before crediting memory.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Headline GAIA result uses repeated passes over the same set, so it is not a clean test of case value.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3 (memory built over 3 iterations on validation; successes and failures both stored); private test 79.40% using the validation case bank. Pass@1 table: GPT-4.1 planner + o3 executor 70.91% avg (L1 77.36, L2 69.77, L3 61.54); o3 planner 63.03%.
limits: Pass@3 with memory built on the same split inflates the figure. Level 3 still weak.
agent_relevance: Treat the 87.88 as an upper bound of in-distribution memory. The 70.91 pass@1 is the honest figure.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: ExpeL keeps a vote-based importance value on each learned insight (ADD starts at 2, UPVOTE or EDIT adds one, DOWNVOTE subtracts one, removed at zero). That is a simple count-based value update, close to a bandit arm counter. Cases are retrieved by task similarity.
numbers: Success: insights-only vs retrieval-only HotpotQA 36% vs 31%; ALFWorld 50% vs 55%; WebShop 37% vs 38%. Both together beat each alone. ExpeL ALFWorld 59.0%; HotpotQA 39.0% vs ReAct 28.0% (ablation table).
limits: Votes are cast by an LLM, not by measured outcomes of use. No exploration scheme. Small test sets (std errors up to 2.1).
agent_relevance: LLM-cast votes are a cheap value signal. A measured outcome after use would be a better reward.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Ablation of how cases are chosen: task-similarity retrieval beat both reasoning-step similarity and random sampling in ALFWorld.
numbers: Text: task-similarity retrieval performs best; reason-similarity slightly lower (changing few-shots within a trajectory is unstable); random sampling a significant drop. Table values printed (garbled): 40.0, 42.5, 48.5 for the weaker variants vs 59.0 for ExpeL.
limits: Mapping of the three weaker values to variants is not certain from the extracted table.
agent_relevance: Random case choice is clearly worse than similarity, so a bandit should start from similarity as a prior, not flat arms.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Stores distilled strategies from both successes and failures (judged by an LLM) and retrieves with plain embedding similarity. The authors say they kept retrieval simple on purpose. Gain over a memory-free agent is consistent.
numbers: WebArena overall success +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 points over memory-free agents on three backbones; up to 20% relative gain and up to 16% fewer steps; SWE-Bench-Verified also improves. Beats Synapse and AWM, which use success-only memory.
limits: Success labels come from an LLM judge, so they are noisy. Gains differ by backbone and shrink for stronger models.
agent_relevance: Failure-derived items help. Evidence for storing negative cases.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: More retrieved experiences hurt: the best setting was one item.
numbers: Ablation by number of retrieved experiences (success rate): 0 -> 39.0; 1 -> 49.7; 2 -> about 46; 3 -> 45.5; 4 -> 44.4.
limits: Single ablation on one backbone and subset; no repeats reported; value for 2 read from a garbled figure.
agent_relevance: Same message as Memento: top-1 to top-2 is the working range. Quantity is not value.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: Keeps a small curated text memory and optionally retrieves similar past items. The ablation separates retrieval alone (DR), curation alone (DC-Cu), and both (DC-RS). Retrieval alone is not reliable.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet: AIME 2024 baseline 23.3, DR 43.3, DC-Cu 50.0, DC-RS 46.7; GPQA-Diamond baseline 59.6, DR 63.6, DC-RS 68.7; MMLU-Pro Eng baseline 61.2, DR 65.2, DC-RS 67.6.
limits: Small test sets (AIME has 30 problems per year, so one problem is 3.3 points). Order of questions matters; one run.
agent_relevance: On strong models curated notes plus retrieval beat verbatim case retrieval. Compact curated entries are the unit that holds value.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: Inside the same paper: verbatim retrieval of past cases (DR) hurt GPT-4o on several tasks, and DC-RS gave no gain on GPQA.
numbers: GPT-4o: Game of 24 baseline 10, DR 6, DC-Cu 93, DC-RS 99. GPQA-Diamond baseline 57.1, DR 55.1, DC-RS 57.1. MMLU-Pro Eng baseline 53.2, DR 48.8, DC-RS 51.2.
limits: Game of 24 gain is one code trick found and reused. The paper says smaller models gain little. Task-specific.
agent_relevance: Retrieval of whole cases can lower accuracy. An agent needs a per-task check that retrieved cases help, and a way to turn them off. This is the bandit null arm.

source: Yan et al. (2026) Memory-R1: Enhancing LLM Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via RL
finding: Learns memory use with RL (PPO or GRPO) from only 152 training QA pairs. An Answer Agent learns to pick the useful items out of 60 retrieved memories (distillation). Outcome reward (exact match) drives it.
numbers: LoCoMo, LLaMA-3.1-8B: GRPO beats the strongest baseline (MemoryOS) by 28.5% F1, 34.0% BLEU-1, 30.2% LLM-judge, relative. PPO: +17.2/+17.6/+19.4. Qwen-2.5-7B: GRPO +24.5/+24.1/+20.0. Distillation ablation GRPO: F1 41.0 -> 45.0, J 60.1 -> 62.7; PPO F1 39.3 -> 41.0.
limits: Memory-style QA benchmarks, not reasoning. Model weights are trained, so this is not a pure scaffold result. Memory-SFT with a GPT-5 teacher was still beaten.
agent_relevance: Learning which retrieved items to use from a tiny outcome-labelled set works. Filtering after retrieval gives 2-4 F1 points.

source: Yan et al. (2026) Memory-R1: Enhancing LLM Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via RL
finding: Reward design matters: a judge-based reward raised judge scores but cut F1 because answers got verbose. Exact-match reward was balanced.
numbers: PPO with LLM-judge reward: F1 33.69, B1 23.36, J 63.58. PPO with exact-match reward: F1 41.05, B1 32.91, J 57.54.
limits: One run per variant as reported.
agent_relevance: Value signals that an LLM can game will be gamed. Use a hard outcome check for case value.

source: Auer, Cesa-Bianchi, Fischer (2002) Finite-time analysis of the multiarmed bandit problem (UCB1)
finding: Classic bandit theory: UCB1 gets logarithmic regret uniformly over time with no prior on rewards. Background for treating each stored case as an arm with an optimism bonus.
numbers: Regret grows as O(log n) in the number of plays n for bounded rewards (from memory, not opened this session).
limits: Assumes fixed arms and stationary rewards. Case banks grow and shift, and a case value depends on the query context, so contextual or non-stationary variants are needed.
agent_relevance: Cite as the design prior for an exploration bonus. Not verified here.

source: Li, Chu, Langford, Schapire (2010) A contextual-bandit approach to personalized news article recommendation (LinUCB)
finding: Contextual bandit with a linear value per arm and an upper confidence bonus, evaluated offline on logged Yahoo data. A standard template for context-dependent item value.
numbers: Not opened this session; I recall click gains over context-free bandits mainly when data are scarce, but give no figure.
limits: Linear payoff assumption. News items, not reasoning cases.
agent_relevance: Template for scoring a case given features of the current problem. Verify before quoting.

source: CASCADE (named in SUBFIELDS.md as the key work for choosing cases by learned value)
finding: I could not open CASCADE or any classic CBR learned-utility retrieval paper: web search quota was used up and scholarly APIs returned rate-limit errors. No numbers given.
numbers: none
limits: Unverified. Do not cite details until a source is opened.
agent_relevance: Gap to fill in a later pass.
